# dsh-doorman
> **Work in progress — not ready for use.** / **开发中，暂不可用。**

An unofficial, community-built plugin for DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
that triages sandbox-escalation app

roval prompts: hard rules, an exact allowlist, and a second-model review,
with the sandbox kept on.
It is not affiliated with DeepSeek.
社区成员独立开发的 dsh 非官方插件：在提权审批弹窗出现前，按“硬性规则 → 精确放行清单 → 第二家模型审查”分流，沙箱始终保持开启。
The current code (stage 3b) runs the hard rules, the allowlist and the model review. By default it o

nly observes: every
prompt still reaches the user, and the plugin logs what it would have done. Auto

mode acts only when all of these hold:
`mode: auto` in the profile, a dsh version the plugin was ch

ecked against and the user confirmed
(`autoModeConfirmedForVersion`), and a session whose permission

preset is `doorman`. Then a hard-rule deny or a model deny
is rejected, a model allow is allowed on

ce (after a snapshot of the outside files it changes), and everything else still
goes to the user —
except in a turn nobody is watching (a scheduled reminder), where it is rejected instead of left wai

ting.
The allowlist only shadows: entries are fingerprinted (exact command, place and the hashes of

the files it depends on) and
what would be added, hit or blocked is logged, but it never allows anyt

hing and `allowlist.json` is never written.
It loads on dsh 0.2.x (`engines.dsh`: `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3

.0-0`) and was checked against the dsh 0.2.0-rc.2,
0.2.1-rc.1 … rc.5 and 0.2.2-rc.1 sources. On 0.2.

2 the new `apply_patch` file tool (off in dsh's shipped bundles) is not
judged: its escalations reac
h the user unchanged.
Turning auto mode on (both edits go in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, which the agent cannot chan
ge; restart dsh after):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
With `defaultPreset: doorman` (the same as choosing “门卫自动审批” under dsh Settings → General → Permissi

on) every new
session starts in that preset; to approve by hand in one session, switch that session

to `workspace-write`. Existing
sessions keep the preset recorded in their own history — switch each

of them once in its permission menu (or type
`/permission doorman`). dsh only applies the default wh

en a session is created, and the plugin does not rewrite
sessions' choices. Sessions on `danger-full

-access` never ask for approval, so the plugin has nothing to judge there.
Without the plugin the do

orman preset behaves exactly like `workspace-write`. Without `defaultPreset` it has to be listed
aft
er `workspace-write`: dsh then gives new sessions the first preset that matches the default sandbox

and approval
policy. The setting cannot ship inside the plugin: a patch layer replaces a row's whole

`config`, and the profile's own
`permission` row, applied last, would override it.
Running other installed plugins' skill scripts is treated like running dsh's own bundled tools; a pl

ain `git push` to a
configured remote is left to the model (force/mirror/delete/ad-hoc-URL pushes ar

e handed to you).
Design notes (Chinese): docs/design.zh.md.
